messages:
Alex: Heads-up, spotted a regression on 8-GPU runs after we flipped LL128 + high channel count as the default. Step time up ~10-15% on ResNet-like microbenchmarks, looks like all-reduce fragmentation and extra startup overhead.

Maria: Can you drop the perf dashboard link so we can eyeball rank variance?

Alex: https://internal.redwood/perf/runs/1749994321 (summary attached below)

perf-bot: profiling summary (auto): run=1749994321, cfg=[8g, fp16, NCCL_PROTO=LL128, NCCL_NCHANNELS=8], step_time=214ms, baseline=193ms, regression=11%

Tanvi: Can you paste an nsys timeline snippet? want to check comm/compute overlap and kernel launch ordering.

Alex: Quick repro command I used locally:
``
export NCCL_PROTO=LL128
export NCCL_ALGO=RING
export NCCL_NCHANNELS=8
export NCCL_DEBUG=WARN
python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc_per_node=8 microbench.py --batch 16 --seq 1024
```

Alex: Condensed nsys timeline I captured:
``
0-60ms   compute (attn fwd) on stream 1
60-80ms  NCCL all-reduce ch0
62-84ms  NCCL all-reduce ch1
... many small 2-8ms all-reduces across channels
82-120ms compute (ffn)
```

Jon: That pattern screams fragmentation. LL128 chops messages into LL packets; with NCHANNELS=8 you multiply the number of small NCCL calls. For small tensors the per-call overhead kills you. Try NCCL_PROTO=LL and fewer channels for small-message patterns.

Samir: Also, double-check kernel stream concurrency. In the trace I saw kernels queued waiting on host launches for other streams which prevents true overlap. Stream priorities and launch ordering matter.

Maria: Interesting — our fused attention kernels reduce compute granularity (more, smaller compute bursts), which makes the workload worse under many small all-reduces.

Tanvi: Proposal: two axes to tune dynamically: (1) proto selection by tensor-size threshold, (2) coalescing small KV syncs across microbatches to reduce distinct all-reduces. Pseudocode:
``
if tensor_bytes < 128KB:
  NCCL_PROTO = 'LL'
  NCCL_NCHANNELS = 2
else:
  NCCL_PROTO = 'LL128'
  NCCL_NCHANNELS = 4
```

Alex: Quick experiment results: NCCL_PROTO=LL + NCCL_NCHANNELS=2 -> step_time=197ms (baseline 193ms). So basically baseline-level latency and ~13% faster than LL128+8 channels. Looks promising for small-message heavy runs.

Jon: For long sequences (seq > 2048) where KV chunks are large, LL128 with ~4 channels gives best sustained bandwidth. So dynamic selection per message size seems right.

Samir: Another lower-risk change: delay non-critical all-reduces until a compute boundary. Accumulate small KV updates and issue a single larger all-reduce per layer-group to amortize startup.

Maria: Can we detect fragmentation from the profiler and flip a runtime flag? e.g., compute avg_nccl_call_duration / avg_tensor_bytes and if > threshold, switch to LL.

Tanvi: I'll prototype a lightweight heuristic in the runtime: maintain a sliding window of recent all-reduce sizes and latencies, then pick proto/channel per-model and optionally per-layer. Keep an override for Dedicated customers.

Alex: Created ticket RI-9873: experiment matrix -> proto=[LL,LL128], nch=[1,2,4,8], batch=[8,16], seq=[512,1024,2048]. Target metrics: p50 step_time, p99 step_time, tail all-reduce latency, bytes/s.

Jon: Add a trace-derived metric: overlap_ratio = time_compute_concurrent_with_nccl / total_compute_time. Target overlap_ratio > 0.6.

Maria: Action items:
- Tanvi: prototype dynamic proto/channel heuristic (1 week)
- Alex: run full matrix on 8g perf-cluster and upload timelines (48h)
- Samir: dig into kernel launch ordering and stream priorities (48h)

Alex: Thanks all. tagging @perf-bot to schedule a re-run after changes. :eyes:

perf-bot: reminder scheduled: re-run experiment matrix in 48h for RI-9873

Samir: One more note — if we do per-layer selection, avoid thrashing NCCL context creation. Prefer reusing communicators with different channel masks instead of full re-init.

Tanvi: Good call, I'll add communicator config caching to the prototype.

Maria: If this works we can expose adaptive defaults in Hosted and an enterprise toggle to pin behavior for Dedicated/Private.

Alex: Closing this thread for now, will post results into RI-9873 once we have runs. :thumbsup:
